q: 1. *The name of first plane landed on the old golf course which makes the present location of Tribhuvan International Airport is
explain: Historical records indicate early flights into the Gauchar golf course involved small gliders/aircraft.

q: 2. Which one is correct sequence with respect to the name of first airport in Nepal?
explain: The airport evolved from a golf course to Gauchar, then named after King Tribhuvan before gaining international status.

q: 3. *International civil aviation organization. (I.C.A.O.) was set up at Montreal
explain: ICAO was formally established on April 4, 1947, following the Chicago Convention.

q: 4. *The minimum length of runway for class ‘C’ type airport is
explain: ICAO classifications designate Class C runway lengths to fall within the 900m to 1500m range.

q: 5. The maximum length and pavement strength of the runway is that of
explain: Code 'A' signifies the longest runway length class, and '1' represents the highest pavement strength.

q: 6. *Runway is designed on the basis of
explain: Structural design of a runway pavement is primarily based on the expected wheel load of the design aircraft.

q: 7. Airport elevation is the reduced level above M.S.L. of ...........
options: highest point of the landing area
lowest point of the landing area
explain: The official elevation of an airport is defined by ICAO as the highest point of the landing area (runways).

q: 8. If all aircraft is flying at a ground speed of 600 km p.h. in air having velocity of 100 km p.h. in the same direction. Compute the air speed of aircraft
explain: Air speed is calculated relative to the air mass; with a headwind, it is the sum of ground and wind speeds.

q: 9. The reduced levels of the ends A and B of a runway are 3025 m and 3035 m and that of its mid-point is 3015 m. The reduced level of the horizontal surface, is ...........
explain: The inner horizontal surface is typically fixed at a height (e.g., 45m) above the airport elevation ($3035 + 45 = 3080$, or $3030$ average $+ 45 = 3075$).

q: 10. An aircraft is flying in an atmosphere of 30°C with a speed of 1234 km ph. Its speed is known as
explain: At 30°C, 1234 km/h is approximately the speed of sound, making the aircraft's speed 'sonic'.

q: 11. For class A Airport the difference of reduced levels of higher and lower edges of the conical surface is ...........
explain: For Class A airports, the conical surface extends to a height of 100m above the inner horizontal surface.

q: 12. The lift off distance is the distance along the centre of the runway between the starting point and ...........
options: point where air craft becomes air borne
point where air craft attains a height of 10.7 m
explain: In airport design manuals, lift-off distance is technically measured to the point where the wheels leave the ground, but for safety calculations, it is often tied to runway length.

q: 13. The meterological condition which influences the size and location of an air port is ...........
explain: Atmospheric pressure and density (affected by temperature and elevation/RL) directly influence engine performance and lift, determining required runway length.

q: 14. The strength of winds is measured with the help of
explain: The Beaufort scale is an empirical measure that relates wind speed to observed conditions at sea or on land.

q: 15. Pick up the correct abbreviation from the following
explain: All listed abbreviations are standard terminology used in aviation and navigation systems.

q: 16. *The lift off distance along the centre of the runway is
options: at a point where aircraft becomes airbone
explain: ICAO defines this as the distance to reach a height of 10.7m (35 ft) above the takeoff surface.

q: 17. If aerodrome reference temperature is 17°C, the net designed length of the runway
explain: Temperature correction is applied after elevation correction to account for air density changes at the site.

q: 18. *The basic length of runway is 600m and RL of the airport is 100m. Actual length of the runway is
19. In question number 58, if temperature at the site is 20°C, then runway length is
explain: Applying the temperature correction (1% per 1°C rise above standard) to the elevation-corrected length results in ~645m.

q: 20. The standard length of the runway is 3000 m. If RL of the airport is 600 m, the design length of the runway is
21. Pick up the correct statement from the following ...........
options: F.I.R. stands for flight information regions
F.I.C. stands for flight information centre
radius of control area is 160 km
explain: These are standard terms and dimensions used in Air Traffic Management (ATM) for regional air space control.

q: 22. The purpose of apron in aircraft is
explain: The apron is the area where aircraft are parked, unloaded or loaded, refueled, or boarded.

q: 23. Apron is used for loading and unloading of passenger while taxiway is
explain: Taxiways are defined paths on an airport connecting runways with aprons and other facilities for taxiing aircraft.

q: 24. Beaufort scale is used to determine ...........
explain: The Beaufort scale is an empirical measure for describing wind intensity based on observed effects.

q: 25. *Flight time refers to
explain: Often called 'block-to-block' time, it starts when an aircraft first moves for takeoff and ends when it stops at the destination gate.

q: 26. *Runway orientation is made so that landing and take off are
explain: Operating against the wind (headwind) provides more lift during takeoff and better braking during landing.

q: 27. Beaufort scale used for measuring wind strength has numerals
explain: The scale typically ranges from 0 (Calm) to 12 (Hurricane force).

q: 28. The engine failure case for determining the basic runway length may require ............
options: either a clearway or a stopway
either a clearway or a stopway or both
explain: In the event of engine failure, the aircraft may need additional distance to either stop safely (stopway) or continue to climb (clearway). The balanced field concept considers both.

q: 29. The minimum width of clearway is ............
explain: According to ICAO standards, the clearway should have a minimum width of 150 m, which is usually centered along the extended centerline of the runway.

q: 30. The coordinates of the ends of a runway are (5000, 5000) and (8000, 7000). The co-ordinates of the A.R.P are
explain: The Airport Reference Point (ARP) is the geometric center. Calculation: (5000+8000)/2 = 6500 and (5000+7000)/2 = 6000.

q: 31. The WCB of the 1st and 2nd end of the runway are 80° and 260° respectively. Find the runway number indicated on the 1st end
explain: The runway number for the 1st end is 80/10 = 8.

q: 32. The maximum number of airports is located in the district
explain: Solukhumbu district has the highest number of airports in Nepal including Lukla and Phaplu.

q: 33. Civil Aviation Authority of Nepal was established in
explain: CAAN was established as an autonomous body on Dec 31, 1998.

q: 34. The number of international airports in Nepal
explain: Nepal recognizes 4 international airports: TIA, GBIA, Pokhara, and Nijgadh (under project).

q: 35. The purposed international airport in Nepal is
explain: Nijgadh International Airport in Bara is the major proposed international airport.

q: 36. Lord Ram returned from Lanka to Ayodhya through
explain: According to Hindu mythology, the Pushpak Viman was used by Lord Ram.

q: 37. The slope of the transitional surface for A, B and C type of runway shall be ............
explain: Transitional surfaces extend from the edge of the runway strip to the inner horizontal surface. For larger categories (A, B, C), the slope is 1:7.

q: 38. *As the temperature of airport increases the runway length
explain: Higher temperature decreases air density, requiring a longer runway length to generate lift.

q: 39. In an airport, if 4 groups of 5 gates each located well-separated are considered for traffic and the future to present traffic ratio is 3, then the total requirement of future gates will be ............
explain: Based on gate occupancy formulas and traffic ratios provided in standard airport engineering textbooks like Khanna and Justo.

q: 40. The landing and take off of an aircraft is made against the direction of wind. In no case the centre line of the runway should make angle with the wind direction exceeding
explain: The runway is oriented to minimize crosswind; a 40-degree angle is a common limit for orientation calculation.

q: 41. The length of the runway under standard atmospheric conditions at site is 1800 m. The design length of runway is, if the actual R.L. of site is 1200 m ............
explain: Applying 7% per 300m elevation: $1200 / 300 = 4$ intervals. $1800 \times (1 + 0.07 \times 4) = 1800 \times 1.28 = 2304$ m.

q: 42. Apron is used for loading/unloading of passenger while taxiway is ............
explain: A taxiway is a path on an airport connecting runways with aprons, hangars, and other facilities, used solely to carry aircraft traffic.

q: 43. *The angle between the longitudinal axis of the fuselage and the horizontal axis is called
explain: Rotation around the lateral axis (nose up/down) is known as the pitch angle.

q: 44. The angle formed by the longitudinal axis of the fuselage and the direction of movement of nose gear
explain: This refers to the castor angle in the landing gear steering geometry.

q: 45. Runway is designed on the basis of ............
explain: While the type of aircraft is important, the specific 'wheel load' (and configuration) is the mechanical basis for structural pavement design.

q: 46. *In the premix asphalt concrete of airport pavement construction aggregate is also heated to
explain: Heating ensures moisture removal and better adhesion of asphalt to the aggregate.

q: 47. *Runway of airport is designed by
explain: Runway design accounts for static aircraft weight, axle loads, and dynamic impact loads.

q: 48. The fastest mode of transport is ............
explain: Air transport provides the highest speeds among all commercial transport modes.

q: 49. *As per ICAO recommendation minimum width of safety area for instrumental runway should is:
explain: For instrument runways, ICAO recommends a minimum safety area width of 300 meters.

q: 50. *I.C.A.O has classifies
explain: ICAO provides classification standards for runway geometry, length, and pavement strength.

q: 51. According to the I.C.A.O. the runway lengths of aerodromes, have been coded by ............
explain: ICAO uses the first few letters (A, B, C, D, E) or numbers (1, 2, 3, 4) depending on the specific code (Reference Code). Answer key marks 'c'.

q: 52. The colour of wind direction indicator is ............
explain: Wind cones (windsocks) are typically high-visibility orange or red, sometimes alternating with white stripes.
